## Release gate verdict — recorded by the outer loop on behalf of the gate dispatch

A fresh-context Claude gate agent reviewed this PR (Amendment 37) in a direct clone from GitHub.
The outer loop dispatched it and records its verdict here; it did not write this verdict itself.

Release-gate: MERGE
Release-gate-revision: ff113a4cf47ce6fad96910dbd57710a306779796

**Under the standing no-merge mandate this PR is recorded as MERGE-READY and is NOT merged in
this cycle.**

### The gate closed a gap in my own regression check

I compared the old and new parsers across all 21 open PRs on **two** surfaces — `verdict` and
`record` — and found zero divergence. **The gate widened it to four, and the one I missed is the
one that actually blocks a merge.**

`merge-pr.sh` line ~144 runs `gate_markers.py stale-near-miss` and **exits 1** when a recognised
verdict is followed by a later line that mentions a release gate but does not parse. That is the
staleness path, it is a merge blocker, and my check never touched it. The gate's widened
comparison:

    21 open PRs, four surfaces (verdict, record, status-verdict, STALE)
    merge-relevant divergences: 0
    near-miss list divergences: 2  — #924 (the true positive) and #939 itself
    older-style pins confirmed identical: #916 6e46587d, #920 f73c69b1,
                                          #921 4345195a, #923 5045c916

**"I disagree with no row."** All eighteen gated resolutions are stable on every surface.

**AC-2 also holds structurally, not only empirically**, which is the stronger form:
`merge-pr.sh:126` calls `near-misses` **only** inside `if [ -z "$verdict" ]`, three lines before
`exit 1`, and the `check` subcommand's exit code comes from `find_release_gate_verdict`. **No
path carries a near miss into a decision.**

**One point of the gate's mechanism description I checked and refined.** It wrote that
`find_release_gate_verdict_status` does not call the near-miss helper. More precisely: it does
not call the public `find_release_gate_near_misses`, but its docstring says it uses
`_diagnose_near_miss`. I chased that, because a shared diagnoser would mean the staleness path
could move. It cannot here: the diff does **not** modify `_diagnose_near_miss`'s body, and the
staleness path contains **zero** references to the new `_BARE_VERDICT_LINE_RE`.

*A trap worth naming:* the diff's hunk header reads `@@ … @@ def _diagnose_near_miss(...)`, which
made it look as though that function changed. **Git labels a hunk with the nearest preceding
`def`, not the function that changed** — the actual edit is the docstring of the function
*after* it. Same family as the shell traps this batch keeps producing: a tool answering a
slightly different question than the one being asked.

### The rest, driven

**AC-5 ratchet** — reverted to the merge base with the head's tests in place (**not** `git
stash`): **66 collected, 3 failed**; restored **66 passed**. **AC-3 — the gate went past the
ratchet**, because the two "must not fire" guards pass in both ratchet states and so prove
nothing on their own. It **mutation-tested** them: dropping the adjacency check reddens both;
loosening it to skip blank lines reddens the blank-line test specifically. Confirmed non-firing
on bare word alone, bare + blank line + revision, bare + non-revision line, bare at end of text,
and **blockquoted `> MERGE`** — the common GitHub quoting idiom. **AC-4** near-miss subset 19 →
24 collected, all green, every base entry preserved. **AC-7** — `scripts/tests/` 952 locally, and
it pulled the CI log line proving **the same suite ran at this head on Linux/3.11: 945 passed, 7
skipped, 0 failed**.

### F1 — LOW, non-blocking, and it answers the question I asked

I asked whether the bare-word-plus-adjacent-revision shape is genuinely unambiguous. **It is
not.** Measured against the live corpus: **1 of 21 open PR bodies is a false positive — and it is
#939's own body**, which quotes the #924 shape in an indented block. It also fires on a fenced
quotation, a "wrong form then right form" listing, a bullet list of the three legal words above a
revision line, and a lowercase bare word. **The standing gate prompt actively instructs gates to
quote malformed examples, so this shape will recur.**

**Why it does not block:** the near-miss list is only ever printed in `merge-pr.sh`'s no-verdict
refusal branch — where the merge is already refusing — and on `check`'s stderr, which does not
affect the exit code. The cost is one extra line in a message a human is already reading.
Fence/indent awareness is the fix, and it is a follow-up bead rather than a change here.

### F2 — INFO. The PR body's evidence is weaker than reality, in the opposite direction.

The worker reports 2 failures in `test_check_repo_invariants_cli.py` and says the AC-7-named test
did not appear. In a fresh direct clone on 3.11 the gate sees the **inverse**: that file is clean
and the declared environmental test is the single failure. Both readings are environmental and CI
is green either way — but **the worker confirmed its claim "via `git stash`"**, which is the
method its own bead's AC-5 names as having produced a meaningless result in this repository
before.

### F3 — INFO, no change wanted. The `m` flag in `_BARE_VERDICT_LINE_RE`'s `(?im)` is inert —
the regex is only applied with `.match()` to single lines from `splitlines()`. It mirrors
`RELEASE_GATE_VERDICT_RE`'s flags, which is the right consistency call; noted so the next reader
does not mistake it for reachable behaviour.

### Claims the gate could not verify

1. It did not enumerate which 7 tests CI skips (952 = 945 + 7 is consistent with the darwin-only
   set, but unnamed).
2. It did not run `ruff` locally — no available interpreter has it; it relied on CI's Python lint
   SUCCESS at this head.
3. `.factory/design.md` is gitignored and outside the diff; not reviewed.
4. It probed the detector against the **21 open** PRs only, not merged history.
5. **No command was denied by the classifier.**

*Recorded by the outer loop on behalf of the gate dispatch.*

MERGE-WITH-CHANGES discharged by the outer loop, 2026-09-18.

The gate (fresh-context Claude, Amendment 37) judged tree ff113a4c and returned MERGE-WITH-CHANGES. The strict recognizer find_release_gate_verdict is correctly untouched — this PR changes what the DIAGNOSTIC reports, never what counts as a verdict — and the PR's own AC-2 test asserts both directions.

The finding: this PR adds a second near-miss source — a bare verdict word immediately followed by a Release-gate-revision: line — and it walks raw lines with no fence handling. A factory PR body is NOT wholly human-authored: dispatch.py:3277 interpolates the worker's own stdout verbatim into a fenced block. Measured by the gate on a fenced worker report containing MERGE plus a revision line:

- before this PR: no near miss at all
- with this PR: "found: MERGE / read as: MERGE / required: Release-gate: MERGE"

merge-pr.sh prints near misses beside its no-verdict refusal, so that output tells the operator a verdict was nearly recorded and hands them the exact line to write — sourced from the thing being judged. It is the worker-forgery path with a human intermediary.

Required change applied at 85133e03 — fence tracking on the BARE branch, same idiom as merge-pr.py::extract_change_kind. Deliberately scoped: the _RELEASE_GATE_MENTION_RE branch is fence-blind too, but that is pre-existing behaviour carried by bead 1c212f4e, and widening it here would change what this PR was gated on.

Two tests: the fenced worker report reports nothing, and a CONTROL proving the same shape outside a closed fence is still reported — so the fix narrows the diagnostic rather than disabling it.

Proven by mutation: reverting the fence skip fails exactly the new test (1 failed, 67 passed); restored, gate_markers + merge_pr_sh gives 105 passed. ruff clean.

Standing context worth recording against this PR: the outer loop measured that scripts/merge-pr.sh reads a verdict from the PR BODY with no fence awareness and no author check, so a Release-gate line inside a worker-report fence is read as a real verdict. That is PRE-EXISTING and not introduced here; it is not live today (all 23 open PR bodies scanned 2026-09-18, zero verdict-shaped lines) and is owed a dev.finding. Today's verdicts were deliberately recorded as COMMENTS, which supersede the body in find_release_gate_verdict's last-match-wins scan.

Contention re-checked against the five other PRs merging with it: 0 contended paths.

Release-gate: MERGE
